newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Water files for Idaho gas rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Water files for Idaho gas rate cut.

text.p: Washington Water Power Co said it filed Monday a request for a natural gas price reduction with the Idaho Public Utilities Commission (IPUC).
If approved by Idaho regulators, WWP said residential gas customers would see their monthly bill decrease by 8.5 percent as of November 1.
The filing primarily reflects decreases from Washington Water Power's suppliers in the cost of gas purchased for use by the company's customers.
WWP said this marks the third straight year it has filed for a natural gas price reduction in the state of Idaho.

"Our focus is on keeping energy prices low, and we've been able to reduce gas prices for our Idaho residential customers by 29 percent in the past three years," said Tom Dukich, manager of rates and tariffs for Washington Water Power.

As the price the utility pays for natural gas rises and falls, the difference between the actual cost of gas purchased for customers and the amount that customers actually pay is accumulated in a special account and refunded or surcharged annually to customers through a filing such as this.
